correctness.rationale: For \(z=x+iy\), the imaginary equation is \(y(3x^2-y^2-(b-a))=0\). Real zeros: exactly one because \(x^3+(a+b)x-1\) strictly increases. Nonreal roots correspond bijectively in conjugate pairs to distinct real roots of \(P(x)=8x^3-2(2b-a)x+1\) satisfying \(3x^2>b-a\); no division at singular thresholds. \(\operatorname{disc}(P)=64[4(2b-a)^3-27]\). For \(b>a\), the negative root always passes the cutoff, and the two positive roots are separated by \(t=\sqrt{(b-a)/3}\) according to the signs of \(E=4(a+2b)^2(b-a)-27\) and \(H=3a-2b\), including strict exclusion at equality. The proof reproduces all 3/5/7 cases and the \((a,b)=(3,5/2)\) open seven-regular-zero witness. Independent \(\operatorname{numpy.roots}\) stationary-root checks on 3000 deterministic positive parameter pairs agreed with the table; these samples supplement the exact cubic argument.
residual_risks: Distinct roots at discriminant zeros, not harmonic multiplicity; constrained strictly to \(a,b>0\), leading coefficient 1, constant -1, analytic degree3 and co-analytic degree1.
Finite sampling does not prove the continuum theorem; real-root sign argument does.
